sources_considered.why: An analyst tally of 2025 capex at the big four hyperscalers, based on company filings. It gives context on the scale of spending.
A secondary report on data centers and GDP growth. Not needed, because the claim's core cannot be adjudicated.
Secondary coverage. It adds nothing beyond context on scale.

receipt.public_excerpt: The four hyperCAPEX companies —Amazon, Google, Meta and Microsoft—collectively spent over $416 billion on CAPEX in 2025 (up 66% from 2024’s $251 billion).

evidence_items.explanation: Shows that the 'enormous expense' part is real in scale. It says nothing on whether the spending rests on a myth, which is the core of the claim.

unresolved_gaps: No evidence can show, as of the evaluation date, whether imminent AGI is a 'myth'. That is the contested premise.
No agreed measure links capex to AGI expectations as opposed to present demand.
